The pilot episode of the American animated television series King of the Hill originally aired on Fox network on Sunday, January 12, 1997. The episode was written by Mike Judge and Greg Daniels, and was directed by Wes Archer. The plot follows a social worker falsely believing that protagonist Hank Hill is abusing his son Bobby.
Plot
Hank and his friends, Dale, Bill, and Boomhauer, attempt to fix Hank's broken red Ford truck. Bobby gets a black eye from getting hit with a baseball at his game. Hank goes to the "Mega Lo Mart" to buy items which he needs to fix his truck. He gets angry at the Mega Lo Mart worker for not knowing where the hardware section is. The town notices Hank's bad temper displayed at the Mega Lo Mart and begin to spread misinformation that Bobby received his black eye from physical abuse from Hank.
A Child Protective Services worker gets notified of the town's suspicions and arrives at Hank's house to do an interview with Hank and his wife Peggy. Hank gets irritated at the social worker and kicks him out of his house. The social worker then asks Dale and Dale's son, Joseph (who is also Bobby's best friend), if Hank had ever abused Bobby, which they deny.
Later, the social worker overhears Bobby and Joseph doing voice impressions of Hank when he kicked the social worker out of the house over the fence, which sounds like Hank threatening and yelling at Bobby. The social worker then rushes back to the Hill house and offers Bobby to have the state take custody of him. Hank chases the social worker back into his car.
Reception
The episode received 19.92 million viewers in the United States.
